configuration.amendment: Added before any v17 learner prediction existed (the four chains started 10:31-10:43 UTC and were mid-way through their first fold): one more ensemble, ens_v17_bag_ctr_c2 (one third LightGBM group, two thirds combination-CatBoost group), and its two candidates at w = 0.6 / 0.7. Reason: a descriptive scan on the recorded v15/v16 fold tables (learner-alone RMSE on the non-LIRF rows, no fitting) puts the best LightGBM share at 0.3-0.4 rather than 0.5: a * ens_v15_lgb + (1 - a) * cat_ctr2 gives 267.84 / 157.78 (seasonal / forward) at a = 0.3 and 268.20 / 157.92 at a = 0.5; with ens_v16_cat instead 268.19 / 158.50 at a = 0.3 and 268.51 / 158.53 at a = 0.5. The bar, the baseline, the learners and every other candidate are unchanged; the candidate count goes from 7 to 9.

ens_v16_bag_60.note: the incumbent v15 recipe; must reproduce the baseline exactly (ratio 1.0); cannot qualify

development_baseline.name: v15 development predictions
development_baseline.recipe: v9 + 1.0 * v12 development residual on matched rows outside LIRF, then (1 - 0.6) * that + 0.6 * ens_v16_bag (out-of-sample per fold) on every row outside LIRF, floored; reproduces 330.814 / 272.538 / 193.272 on Jan / Jul / Nov 2025 (runs/adsb_v16_v2/selection.json, ens_v16_bag_60)

configuration.development_scheme: leave-one-month-out over the three scoring months that hold out-of-sample v9 predictions (Jan and Jul 2025 from the seasonal fold, Nov 2025 from the forward fold); for each variant (scope, feature set) the residual model is fitted on the other two months' in-scope rows and applied to the held-out month's in-scope rows; every other row keeps v9

ens_v16_bag.rule: as declared in configs/adsb_v16_v1.json (mean of the six-LightGBM group mean ens_v15_lgb and the five-CatBoost group mean ens_v16_cat; runs/adsb_v16/ens_v16_bag, hash-bound below); the v15 learner table and the baseline here

ens_v17_bag.rule: mean of the two group means

ens_v17_bag_c2.rule: one third of the LightGBM group mean plus two thirds of the CatBoost group mean

ens_v17_bag_ctr.rule: mean of the two group means

ens_v17_bag_ctr_c2.rule: one third of the LightGBM group mean plus two thirds of the combination-CatBoost group mean (amendment)

ens_v17_cat.rule: mean of finite predictions (the five earlier CatBoosts and the four new ones)

ens_v17_ctr.rule: mean of finite predictions (the five CatBoosts with categorical combinations: cat_ctr2 and the four new ones)

ens_v17_new.rule: mean of finite predictions (the four new CatBoosts; descriptive)

ensembles.missing_members: if a learner variant fails to complete on all three folds it is dropped from every ensemble that lists it and the drop is recorded in the selection; no other change
ensembles.tool: tools/ensemble_adsb_full.py (per-row mean of finite member predictions, fold by fold); nested means are built by listing members with multiplicities that reproduce the weighted group means exactly (ens_v17_bag: each of the six LightGBMs three times and each of the nine CatBoosts twice; ens_v17_bag_ctr: each LightGBM five times and each of the five CTR CatBoosts six times; ens_v17_bag_c2: each LightGBM three times and each of the nine CatBoosts four times); every learner predicts every non-LIRF row; ens_v17_bag_ctr_c2: each LightGBM five times and each of the five CTR CatBoosts twelve times (90 entries)

execution.learner_fits_on_workers: tools/launch_adsb_learners.py --config configs/adsb_v17_v1.json (16 threads per fit, one variant per worker, folds in sequence)

external_data.extraction: tools/adsb_extract_day.py keeps positions inside the ten aerodrome boxes that are on the ground or below 3,000 ft; per-day parquet with archive part hashes under data/external/adsblol/surface/ (the tool now skips and counts a corrupt archive member instead of aborting the day; the surface files used here predate that change and are unaffected)
external_data.license: Open Database License (ODbL) 1.0; feeder data CC0; licence files are inside every archive
external_data.matching: tools/build_adsb_features.py: ICAO callsign (CALLSIGN_flt, else FLIGHT_mvt) and takeoff within the track's ground-to-air transition; stand positions learned label-free from covered segments of Jan/Mar/Apr/Jul/Nov 2025 (1,111 stands); the pass-2 matches and stands are exactly the v11 inputs, snapshotted under data/external/adsblol/matches_v11/ and hash-bound below
external_data.source: adsb.lol globe_history daily archives (GitHub releases adsblol/globe_history_2025 and globe_history_2026, tags vYYYY.MM.DD-planes-readsb-prod-0)

configuration.floor_seconds_rule: minimum departure label over the refit months (-12), applied after the residual

incumbent.official_rank: not recorded (the user's standing rule: no leaderboard checks)
incumbent.recipe: v15 = (1 - 0.6) * (v9 + 1.0 * v12 ADS-B residual on matched rows outside LIRF) + 0.6 * ens_v16_bag (mean of the six-LightGBM group mean and the five-CatBoost group mean, all without LIRF) on every row outside LIRF, floored (configs/adsb_v16_v2.json, ens_v16_bag_60; uploaded 10:13 UTC 16 September 2026)

learner_common.catboost_base: configs/timeline_v1.json catboost block (depth 8, learning rate 0.055, l2 10, Bernoulli 0.8, rsm 0.9, max_ctr_complexity 1, one_hot_max_size 10, early stopping 200) with the overrides above and a 20,000-round cap
learner_common.features: timeline bundle CORE + FLOWN + SURFACE (276) + 27 ADS-B features from data/external/adsblol/matches (matches2_*, stands.parquet: exactly the tables the v14 learners used; hashes recorded in every run record)
learner_common.folds: seasonal and forward (out-of-sample fold predictions), refit on the eleven 2025 months at the median best iteration
learner_common.settings: configs/timeline_v1.json (lightgbm / catboost blocks; parameter overrides above)

cat_ctr2_d10.note: two-way combinations at depth 10 (the two v16 structure changes together)

cat_ctr2_oh2.note: two-way combinations with one-hot encoding limited to binary categoricals, so that airport (10 values, one-hot at the default 10 and therefore excluded from CatBoost combinations) enters the target statistics and the combinations: 49% of the runway codes and 53% of the stand codes are shared by more than one airport (Nov 2025 departures), so the plain runway and stand CTRs pool airports

cat_ctr2_s17.note: the v16 cat_ctr2 recipe (two-way categorical combinations) with a new seed: the strongest single v16 learner, bagged

cat_ctr3.note: three-way categorical combinations (e.g. stand x runway x operator); otherwise the cat_ctr2 recipe and seed

learner_code_run_adsb_learner.note: the runner as amended in v16 (matched-row RMSE None when no finite prediction); snapshot docs/adsb_v17/run_adsb_learner_declared.py

configuration.prior_evidence: Declared after adsb_v16 (docs/adsb_v16/README.md): the two structural CatBoosts moved the development mean ratio to v14 from 0.99786 (v15 bag) to 0.99712 (ens_v16_bag), and the export scored 242.5783 officially (v14 243.5805). cat_ctr2 (max_ctr_complexity 2) alone matched the whole v15 bag on the non-LIRF rows (268.84 / 159.60 seasonal / forward against 268.81 / 159.18), cat_d10 was weaker (270.49 / 161.97) and the five-CatBoost group mean (269.17 / 160.30) is behind cat_ctr2 alone, so the CatBoost group is diluted by its weaker members; the nine airport specialists added nothing and are not carried forward. The four learners here are all of the categorical-combination kind: a second cat_ctr2 seed, three-way combinations, combinations at depth 10 and combinations with the airport code admitted to the target statistics (one_hot_max_size 2). The ensembles test three ways of weighting them: all nine CatBoosts against the six LightGBMs (ens_v17_bag), only the combination CatBoosts against the LightGBMs (ens_v17_bag_ctr) and the CatBoost group at two thirds (ens_v17_bag_c2). No learner listed here had been fitted before this declaration. Diagnostics closed on evidence on 16 September and disclosed in docs/adsb_v15/README.md and docs/adsb_v16/README.md: LIRF residual, LIRF fill mixture, first-point geometry, blend structure, complete-match scope, callsign fallback matching, airport specialists.

residual_model.applies_to: the residual model is exactly v12's (nb feature set, matched rows outside LIRF, weight 1.0); each candidate then blends the result with a declared ensemble, value = (1 - w) * (v9 + residual) + w * ensemble, on every row outside LIRF; rows outside both scopes keep v9 exactly.
residual_model.blend: post-hoc convex combination with the extra table adsb_full (candidate_values in tools/run_adsb_v11.py); a NaN learner value leaves the row unblended
residual_model.prediction: v9 + weight * residual on in-scope rows, then floor
residual_model.rounds_rule: development: rounds per held-out month and variant (scope, feature set) come from a 5-fold day-grouped inner split of the two training months (median best iteration, 200 rounds patience, at most 4000); the held-out month is never used for rounds; export: median of the selected variant's three development round counts

scopes.all_no_lirf: every departure at any airport except LIRF: a blend scope only (unmatched rows there become (1 - w) * v9 + w * adsb_full)
scopes.matched_no_lirf: departures with a matched ADS-B surface segment at any airport except LIRF (adsb_matched == 1 and airport != LIRF): the residual model's training and prediction scope (exactly v12)

configuration.selection: For each candidate (ensemble, blend weight w), RMSE of the blended prediction on each held-out month versus the v15 development prediction (the incumbent's recipe on the same rows: all departures of the month). A candidate is eligible when it is not worse than v15 on ANY month (ratio <= 1.0) and its mean ratio over the three months is at most 0.9985 (a 0.15% mean improvement over the incumbent). Choose the eligible candidate with the lowest mean ratio to v15; otherwise select nothing. The bar is set before any v17 learner is fitted: v16 added two CatBoosts to the v15 ensemble for a 0.074-point gain in the mean ratio to v14 (0.99786 -> 0.99712), and this round adds four CatBoosts of the kind that produced that gain; 0.15% is roughly twice the width of a single month's paired-day interval divided by the month RMSE, so a qualifying candidate improves every month by a margin that the day-level noise does not explain. The ens_v16_bag_60 candidate reproduces the incumbent and is a check, not a candidate that can qualify. Ratios to v9, per-airport tables and the paired-day bootstrap interval of the RMSE difference to v15 are descriptive only.
